To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed ABX-EGFr, a human Ig2 monoclonal anti-EGF-receptor antibody, which inhibits the binding of EGF and TGF-alpha to EGFR-expressing human tumor cell lines, and blocks EGF-induced tumor cell activation and proliferation.

a human monoclonal antibody specific for human epidermal growth receptor (EGFr), which blocks the binding of the growth factor to the receptor, inhibits EGFr-dependent tumor cell activation and growth, and completely eradicates well-established tumors without any concomitant chemotherapy.
ABX-EGFr, a human Ig2 monoclonal anti-EGFr antibody generated by XenoMouse technology has potent anti-tumor effects on EGFr expressing tumor xenograft models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a humanized monoclonal antibody against human EGFR, a growth factor receptor that is over-expressed in many human tumors.
the development of a novel class of cancer therapeutics based on the use of fully human antibodies that target the growth factor receptors.
the discovery, optimization and development of fully human antibodies to the EGF receptor (EGFr).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this is a very promising antibody and it has the potential to become the first anti-EGFr antibody to be used clinically.
the results obtained with ABX- EGFr demonstrate the therapeutic potential of EGFr-directed mAbs for the treatment of human solid tumors that express high levels of EGFr.
ABX-EGFR has the potential to become a very effective therapeutic antibody for the treatment of a variety of human cancers that express high levels of EGFR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the XenoMouse technology has been used successfully to generate fully human antibodies against human EGFr and that the anti-tumor activity in vivo is superior to any other anti-EGF antibody reported in the literature.
we have generated a human antibody to human EGFr that has potent anti-tumor effects.
we have generated a fully human anti EGFR mAb (ABX-EGF) that is highly potent in inhibiting the growth of multiple EGFR overexpressing tumor xenograft models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ABX-EGFR, a human monoclonal antibody that blocks the interaction of EGFR with its ligands, is an effective therapeutic agent for the treatment of solid tumors that express EGFR.
ABX-EGFr, a fully human antibody specific for EGFR, can be used for cancer therapy.
